findings.claim: The machine-readable verification gate cannot fail for four of the five modules it claims to cover. Both `test_command` and `build_command` are bare `for m in engine tui tools/deterministic-check-runner tools/entry-contract-validator tools/review-preflight; do (cd "$m" && ...); done` loops with no `set -e`, no `|| exit`, and no failure accumulator. A POSIX `for` loop exits with the status of the last command executed, so `test_exit_code: 0` and `build_exit_code: 0` are satisfied whenever `tools/review-preflight` alone succeeds — a failure in `engine`, `tui`, `tools/deterministic-check-runner`, or `tools/entry-contract-validator` is silently discarded. This is a structurally-unfailable gate reported as a pass, the exact defect class this change's own Batch 8 exists to eliminate ("a tautological check reported as 'verified' is a fabricated assurance"), reproduced in the change's own verification record. The pasted per-package `ok` lines mitigate for a human reader but are not what the recorded exit code asserts, and the same loop form is what apply-progress relies on for every batch's "full suite green" claim.

findings.claim: The recorded `test_output_hash` cannot be re-derived by anyone, so it does not function as the durable evidence anchor it is presented as. It hashes `go test` output, which embeds per-package wall-clock durations that vary run to run — demonstrated within this candidate, where the identical command's output is pasted eight times with eight different duration sets (for example `engine/installer` at 6.004s, 5.998s, 6.310s, 3.611s, 6.062s, 6.086s, 6.073s, 5.995s). findings.claim: The recorded `test_output_hash` cannot be re-derived by anyone, so it does not function as the durable evidence anchor it is presented as. It hashes `go test` output, which embeds per-package wall-clock durations that vary run to run — demonstrated within this candidate, where the identical command's output is pasted eight times with eight different duration sets (for example `engine/installer` at 6.004s, 5.998s, 6.310s, 3.611s, 6.062s, 6.086s, 6.073s, 5.995s). A verifier re-running the same command on the same tree gets a different hash, so the field can only ever confirm "this exact captured text", never "this tree passes". The same defect applies to the `--evidence-revision` values apply-progress records at settle time (Batch 9's `sha256:2c5aa0cd…`, described as "hash of the full test-suite output above"; Batch 10's `sha256:5825df55…`), which are the values the attempt ledger retains as proof.

findings.claim: The instrument this change ships has never been executed end to end even once, and the candidate nonetheless records "Archive-ready: YES". Task 6.3 — this change's own closure, the single task that runs the t0/t1 resolution, the anchor verification, and the record write together against real data — remains unchecked across all ten batches and eight verify rounds, deferred as structurally impossible before merge. Everything actually proven is proven by proxy: string pins over shipped prose, a `resolveD2T1` reimplementation that lives only in `_test.go` and is not the code any pipeline runs, and two committed fixtures mirroring hand-reconstructed historical records. That is a coherent and honestly-disclosed position, but it means no assertion anywhere in this candidate observes the shipped instrument producing a value; the first real execution will be the archive of this change itself, with no round scheduled to inspect the result.

findings.claim: `build_output_hash: sha256:e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855` is the SHA-256 of the empty string. It is the correct hash for a silent successful build, but as an evidence field it cannot discriminate between all five modules building cleanly and the build command never having run — any no-output outcome produces the identical value. The real signal is carried entirely by `build_exit_code`, which is itself weakened by the unguarded loop (see the CRITICAL at openspec/changes/sdd-cycle-timestamp-instrumentation/verify-report.md:9-13). Recording a per-module marker, or hashing the list of produced binaries, would make this field able to fail.
